body.statement: Using \(\mathrm{def{:}shrinking\mbox{-}margin\mbox{-}handle}\), characterize the sharp rate frontier for cell-probability or score-boundary margins \(m_n\downarrow0\): for each admissible baseline array \(B\), determine necessary and sufficient relations between \(m_n\) and \(\eta_n(B)\) for conditional sampling-cdf, data-dependent zero-null reference-cdf, quantile, and local-power transfer, and construct a finite-population sequence showing failure below that frontier.
body.justification: The fixed positive-margin theorem leaves the scientifically relevant boundary where recruitment cells become rare or rankings unstable.
body.gap: Tian and Taylor require selection-likelihood control, while available post-selection nonuniformity results do not identify the without-replacement enrichment boundary.
body.consumer: The frontier would tell trial planners how close a recruitment threshold may approach an estimated score boundary before Gaussian power calculations cease to be reliable.
